text:
Jackson Blake, a fourth-round pick in 2021, is having the season that turns a depth winger into a core piece. He has a point in nine straight games, 19 in 19, and is on the ice for 83% of Carolina's power-play time after 40% last season. His ice time is up to almost 18 minutes a night.

The underlying play backs it. Carolina gets 65% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, eight points better than without him, and The Hockey Writers have noticed the chemistry with Logan Stankoven. His own chances are up too.

If anything, the goals are behind: 5 on 7.8 expected, shooting about 10%. The assists may run a little hot (his point pace sits above our range), but the chances say his goal total should catch up. Evolving-Hockey liked his play-driving last season (93rd percentile), with the caveat that he skates with strong teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts his home-plate chances in the 88th percentile. Watch the power play: he's on it now, and that's where the next step lives.
headline: Jackson Blake has moved up, and he's earning it
